outlooks.summary: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS ARE LIKELY ACROSS PARTS OF THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY TO NORTH DAKOTA AND PART OF SOUTH DAKOTA...MAINLY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. A TORNADO THREAT AND VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH STORMS IN CENTRAL MINNESOTA...WHILE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS ACROSS THE REST OF THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. A FEW STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST STATES.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MODELS ARE IN AGREEMENT SHOWING A VIGOROUS SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL TRACK FROM THE NRN ROCKIES ALONG THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER REACHING WRN ND BY 12Z THURSDAY...WITH A TRAILING POSITIVELY-ORIENTED TROUGH EXTENDING ACROSS THE NORTHWESTERN STATES. AS THIS OCCURS...HEIGHTS ARE EXPECTED TO RISE DOWNSTREAM ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY AND GREAT LAKES. MEANWHILE...A MIDLEVEL PERTURBATION...CURRENTLY MOVING EWD THROUGH WY PER WATER-VAPOR IMAGERY...WILL TRACK EWD AMIDST THE HEIGHT RISES REACHING CENTRAL MN BY 04/00Z. AT THE SURFACE...A CYCLONE...ATTENDANT TO THE NRN ROCKIES SHORTWAVE TROUGH...WILL TRACK EWD FROM CENTRAL MT THROUGH ND...WITH A TRAILING COLD FRONT ACCELERATING EAST OVER THE NRN PLAINS AFTER 04/00Z. FARTHER E/SE...A WARM FRONT WILL ADVANCE NNEWD FROM THE MID-MO VALLEY TODAY...AND SHOULD EXTEND FROM CENTRAL-SERN ND THROUGH CENTRAL MN TO NRN IL BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING.

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: A CLUSTER OF ELEVATED TSTMS SHOULD BE ONGOING AT 12Z/ ACROSS PARTS OF ERN SD...SWRN MN AND NWRN IA DRIVEN BY LOW-LEVEL WAA WELL N OF THE WARM FRONT...AND ALONG THE LEADING EXTENT OF AN EXPANDING EML ACROSS THE PLAINS. THIS CONVECTION MAY BE SUSTAINED THROUGH THE MORNING ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL/SRN MN WITH A MARGINAL HAIL RISK ON THE FRINGE OF LARGER BUOYANCY. GIVEN THE OCCURRENCE OF THIS ACTIVITY...A PRONOUNCED DIFFERENTIAL HEATING CORRIDOR COULD DEVELOP...POTENTIALLY INVOF OF THE WARM FRONTAL POSITION INTO CENTRAL MN BY LATE AFTERNOON. STRONG POTENTIAL INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR CHARACTERIZED BY UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S SURFACE DEW POINTS BENEATH STEEPENING MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES RESULTING IN MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG. DESPITE THE WEAK 500-MB HEIGHT RISES THROUGH THIS PERIOD ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY...DIFFLUENT UPPER-LEVEL FLOW IN CONJUNCTION WITH PERSISTENT LOW-LEVEL WAA AND ASCENT ATTENDANT TO THE WY PERTURBATION SHOULD FOSTER SUFFICIENT ASCENT FOR NEW STORM INITIATION DURING THE MID-LATE AFTERNOON ON THE PERIPHERY OF THE EML/CAPPING INVERSION. DEEP-LAYER SHEAR INCREASING TO 45-55 KT THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE MN/WI PORTION OF THE SLIGHT RISK WILL BE QUITE FAVORABL

sections.title: ND/NRN AND ERN SD
sections.text: MODELS CONTINUE TO SHOW LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL BE INCREASING AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING COLD FRONT...BUT SHOULD BE COMPARATIVELY SLOWER TO RETURN RELATIVE TO MN. HOWEVER...FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE ROBUST IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE NRN ROCKIES SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ACCELERATING COLD FRONT. THIS SHOULD ALLOW INITIAL STORMS TO FORM LATE THIS AFTERNOON NEAR THE MT/ND BORDER WITHIN A MARGINALLY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT. ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY THIS EVENING AS IT SPREADS EWD INTO INCREASINGLY RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE/STRONGER INSTABILITY. SEVERE HAIL AND STRONG WINDS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS AS THE COLD FRONT ADVANCES TOWARD THE MN BORDER.

sections.title: ERN AL/GA/SC/NC/SRN VA
sections.text: STRONG SURFACE HEATING WITHIN A VERY MOIST AIR MASS /PW VALUES RANGING FROM 1.75-2 INCHES/ WILL RESULT IN MODERATE INSTABILITY ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST STATES. ALTHOUGH DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL BE WEAK...LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH MAINLY PULSE-TYPE STORMS. ..PETERS/SMITH.. 09/03/2014

outlooks.summary: A FEW TORNADOES...VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT ACROSS CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL WISCONSIN. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS EVENING INTO TONIGHT FROM NORTHEAST MONTANA INTO NORTH DAKOTA.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A STRONG MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL MOVE EWD FROM THE NRN ROCKIES THIS MORNING TO CENTRAL/ERN MT BY THIS EVENING AND ND OVERNIGHT. AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE CYCLONE WILL DEVELOP FROM SE MT TO NW SD BY THIS EVENING...AND THEN EWD TO THE W CENTRAL MN BORDER BY THE END OF THE PERIOD. IN ADVANCE OF THE CYCLONE...A WARM/MOIST AIR MASS WILL SPREAD NWD WITH THE SURFACE WARM FRONT IN SW MN/ERN SD THIS AFTERNOON...AND MOISTURE WILL ALSO SPREAD NWWD TOWARD WRN ND. A MORE SUBTLE MID-UPPER SPEED MAX WILL ALSO EJECT ENEWD FROM ERN WY TO MN BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON AS THE WARM FRONT REACHES THE I-94 CORRIDOR IN MN.

sections.title: MN AREA THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: THE OBSERVED UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS IN KS/NEB WILL SPREAD QUICKLY NWD TODAY AND BE AUGMENTED BY EVAPOTRANSPIRATION BENEATH AN ELEVATED MIXED LAYER...RESULTING IN STRONG DESTABILIZATION FROM ERN SD INTO CENTRAL MN WHERE MLCAPE COULD EXCEED 3000 J/KG. THE BASE OF THE ELEVATED MIXED LAYER WILL BE WARM ENOUGH TO REQUIRE SURFACE TEMPERATURES AOA 90 F TO MINIMIZE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION. STILL...THE LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME AND THE APPROACH OF THE SPEED MAX FROM NE WY COULD PROVIDE SUFFICIENT ASCENT TO SUPPORT THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE WARM FRONT IN CENTRAL MN...IN THE WAKE OF THE MORNING ELEVATED CONVECTION. THE STORM ENVIRONMENT WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS WITH A RISK FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES WITH THE INITIAL WARM FRONTAL STORMS. BY THIS EVENING...CONVECTION SHOULD GROW UPSCALE INTO A CLUSTER AND MOVE EWD/ESEWD INTO WI WITH A CONTINUING DAMAGING WIND/LARGE HAIL RISK.

sections.title: NE MT AND ND THIS EVENING INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL BE MARGINAL INITIALLY...BUT WILL TEND TO SPREAD WWD INTO WRN ND BY LATE AFTERNOON. THIS MOISTENING WILL OCCUR BENEATH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AOA 8 C/KM...AND IMMEDIATELY IN ADVANCE OF THE SURFACE COLD FRONT AND THE BELT OF STRONGER ASCENT PRECEDING THE MIDLEVEL TROUGH OVER ERN MT. ASSUMING THE LOW-MID 60S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS NOW ENTERING S CENTRAL SD CAN REACH WRN ND BY LATE AFTERNOON WITHOUT MIXING OUT...MLCAPE COULD REACH 2000 J/KG. STORMS THAT DEVELOP IN THE 22-00Z TIME FRAME ACROSS NE MT WILL ENCOUNTER INCREASING BUOYANCY WITH EWD EXTENT...AND FAVORABLE DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR FOR BOTH SUPERCELLS AND ORGANIZED BOWING SEGMENTS. THESE STORMS WILL PERSIST WELL INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS ACROSS ND...WITH AN ATTENDANT RISK FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ..THOMPSON/MOSIER.. 09/03/2014

outlooks.summary: A FEW TORNADOES...VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT ACROSS CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL WISCONSIN. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS EVENING INTO TONIGHT FROM NORTHEAST MONTANA INTO NORTH DAKOTA. MORNING UA ANALYSIS SHOWS A DEEPENING UPPER TROUGH OVER THE NORTHWEST STATES. LIFT AHEAD OF THIS TROUGH OVER THE NORTHERN PLAINS WILL RESULT IN SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS OVER WESTERN SD...WITH A WARM FRONT EXTENDING EASTWARD ACROSS PARTS OF SD/MN. THIS BOUNDARY WILL BE THE FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH TONIGHT.

sections.title: MN/WI
sections.text: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING THIS MORNING OVER SOUTH-CENTRAL MN IN REGION OF ENHANCED LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. THESE STORMS MAY PERSIST WITH A MARGINAL HAIL RISK THROUGH THE EARLY AFTERNOON. MEANWHILE...STRONG HEATING AND MOISTENING TO THE SOUTHWEST OF THE EARLY CONVECTION WILL HELP TO WEAKEN CAP AND LEAD TO NEW VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY OVER WESTERN MN BY LATE AFTERNOON. THESE STORMS WILL BE IN A REGION OF STRONG MLCAPE /OVER 3000 J/KG/ AND FAVORABLE EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES FOR SUPERCELL STORMS. LOW LEVEL SHEAR IN VICINITY OF WARM FRONT AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES MAY BE SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW TORNADOES...ALONG WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THESE STORMS ARE FORECAST BY MOST 12Z CAMS TO ORGANIZE UPSCALE INTO A BOWING LINE THAT TRACKS EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS PARTS OF WI TONIGHT...WHERE AN ENHANCED RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS IS FORECAST.

sections.title: MT/SD
sections.text: SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT AND NORTH OF THE DEVELOPING LOW WILL HELP TO TRANSPORT 50S/60S DEWPOINTS INTO PARTS OF NORTHEAST MT AND MUCH OF ND. STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND APPROACHING UPPER TROUGH WILL HELP TO YIELD A CORRIDOR OF AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF AROUND 1000 J/KG. THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM ALONG THIS AXIS BY LATE AFTERNOON AND TRACK ALONG/NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT ACROSS ND THIS EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW SUBSTANTIAL VERTICAL SHEAR...FAVORABLE FOR DISCRETE SUPERCELLS. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE. ..HART/ROGERS.. 09/03/2014

outlooks.summary: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED LATE THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT ACROSS PARTS OF THE UPPER MIDWEST AND NORTHERN GREAT PLAINS. A FEW TORNADOES...VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: MN/WI
sections.text: CONVECTION HAS PERSISTED WITHIN CONTINUED LOW-LEVEL WAA ACROSS CNTRL MN. ABUNDANT STRATOCUMULUS IS STILL EVIDENT WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR S OF THIS ACTIVITY LIMITING DESTABILIZATION. STILL...CONVERGENCE SHOULD REMAIN ROBUST OVER PORTIONS OF THE UPPER MN VALLEY WHERE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW IS MODULATING THE EFFECTIVE WARM FRONT. WITH LARGE-SCALE ASCENT PERHAPS ENHANCED BY THE NEXT IN A SERIES OF SUBTLE IMPULSES /EVIDENT IN WATER VAPOR IMAGERY ACROSS CNTRL SD/...VIGOROUS SURFACE-BASED DEVELOPMENT REMAINS PROBABLE OVER W-CNTRL MN BY EARLY EVENING. SEE PREVIOUS DISCUSSION FOR EXPECTED CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION INTO TONIGHT.

sections.title: NRN GREAT PLAINS
sections.text: SURFACE DEW POINTS ARE GRADUALLY RECOVERING...BUT REMAIN IN THE MIDDLE 40S TO MIDDLE 50S ACROSS MOST OF ERN MT INTO WRN/CNTRL ND. THE LEADING EDGE OF RICHER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE DEW POINTS AOA THE MIDDLE 60S HAS REACHED FAR S-CNTRL ND AND CNTRL/ERN SD BENEATH A STOUT EML/CAPPING INVERSION. CONVECTION JUST AHEAD OF THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH SHOULD INCREASE IN COVERAGE ACROSS ERN MT INTO WRN ND BY 00Z WITH LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED SEVERE WIND AS THE PRIMARY INITIAL RISKS. DURING THE EVENING...SOME OF THIS ACTIVITY MAY FURTHER INTENSIFY AS IT INTERCEPTS THE PLUME OF RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE. VERY LARGE HAIL AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES MAY OCCUR WITH DISCRETE SUPERCELLS THAT TRANSITION TO SMALL-SCALE BOWS OVERNIGHT. ..GRAMS.. 09/03/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1119 AM CDT WED SEP 03 2014/ MORNING UA ANALYSIS SHOWS A DEEPENING UPPER TROUGH OVER THE NORTHWEST STATES. LIFT AHEAD OF THIS TROUGH OVER THE NORTHERN PLAINS WILL RESULT IN SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS OVER WESTERN SD...WITH A WARM FRONT EXTENDING EASTWARD ACROSS PARTS OF SD/MN. THIS BOUNDARY WILL BE THE FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH TONIGHT.

sections.title: MN/WI
sections.text: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING THIS MORNING OVER SOUTH-CENTRAL MN IN REGION OF ENHANCED LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. THESE STORMS MAY PERSIST WITH A MARGINAL HAIL RISK THROUGH THE EARLY AFTERNOON. MEANWHILE...STRONG HEATING AND MOISTENING TO THE SOUTHWEST OF THE EARLY CONVECTION WILL HELP TO WEAKEN CAP AND LEAD TO NEW VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY OVER WESTERN MN BY LATE AFTERNOON. THESE STORMS WILL BE IN A REGION OF STRONG MLCAPE /OVER 3000 J/KG/ AND FAVORABLE EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES FOR SUPERCELL STORMS. LOW LEVEL SHEAR IN VICINITY OF WARM FRONT AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES MAY BE SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW TORNADOES...ALONG WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THESE STORMS ARE FORECAST BY MOST 12Z CAMS TO ORGANIZE UPSCALE INTO A BOWING LINE THAT TRACKS EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS PARTS OF WI TONIGHT...WHERE AN ENHANCED RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS IS FORECAST.

sections.title: MT/SD
sections.text: SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT AND NORTH OF THE DEVELOPING LOW WILL HELP TO TRANSPORT 50S/60S DEWPOINTS INTO PARTS OF NORTHEAST MT AND MUCH OF ND. STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND APPROACHING UPPER TROUGH WILL HELP TO YIELD A CORRIDOR OF AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF AROUND 1000 J/KG. THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM ALONG THIS AXIS BY LATE AFTERNOON AND TRACK ALONG/NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT ACROSS ND THIS EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW SUBSTANTIAL VERTICAL SHEAR...FAVORABLE FOR DISCRETE SUPERCELLS. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONGOING ELEVATED TSTMS ACROSS CNTRL MN ARE LIKELY TO PERSIST FOR AT LEAST THE NEXT 2-3 HRS...POSING A THREAT FOR ISOLATED SVR HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS. WHILE A WW IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED IN THE NEAR-TERM...A MORE SUBSTANTIAL SVR THREAT IS FORECAST TO MATERIALIZE BY LATE AFTERNOON...AND WILL LIKELY REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: PERSISTENT LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME CONTINUES TO MAINTAIN ELEVATED CONVECTION ALONG THE LLJ NOSE ACROSS CNTRL PORTIONS OF MN EARLY THIS AFTERNOON. DESPITE BEING POSITIONED ALONG THE ERN EDGE OF AN EML PLUME CENTERED OVER THE NRN PLAINS...TSTMS HAVE SHOWN OCCASIONAL ORGANIZED STRUCTURES /GIVEN 30-40 KT OF CLOUD-LAYER SHEAR/ AND POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL...WITH BRIEF UPWARD PULSES IN WDSS-2 MESH LOOPS NOTED. CURRENT TRENDS SUGGEST ELEVATED TSTMS AND AN ASSOCIATED HAIL THREAT WILL PERSIST AT LEAST THE NEXT COUPLE HRS...WITH ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT POTENTIALLY FURTHER ENCOURAGED BY A WEAK IMPULSE MOVING ACROSS CNTRL SD AS OF 1700Z. MEANWHILE...POOL OF RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WITH LOW-70S F DEWPOINTS IS NOW ENTERING SWRN MN...AND IS FORECAST TO CONTINUE ADVECTING NWD THIS AFTERNOON IN CONJUNCTION WITH A SYNOPTIC WARM FRONT. POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING SHOULD EVENTUALLY GIVE WAY TO SFC-BASED TSTMS...PERHAPS IN THE 21-23Z TIME PERIOD. AS THIS OCCURS...AN INCREASING THREAT FOR DMGG WIND GUSTS...LARGE HAIL...AND A FEW TORNADOES IS EXPECTED...WHICH WILL LIKELY REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE LATER THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLD LARGE HAIL APPEARS TO BE THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS ACROSS CNTRL PORTIONS OF MN. THIS ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY MOVE INTO NWRN WI BY EARLY EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY THIS AFTERNOON IMPLIES A SUBTLE DISTURBANCE IS MOVING ACROSS E-CNTRL SD WITH THIS FEATURE MOVING TOWARDS THE SRN HALF OF MN THIS EVENING. VISIBLE SATELLITE CONTINUES TO SHOW EXTENSIVE LOW CLOUDS BENEATH A STOUT CAP/ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AS STRONG H85-H7 WARM AIR ADVECTION AIDS IN ELEVATED STORM DEVELOPMENT N OF A SURFACE WARM FRONT OVER SRN MN INTO CNTRL WI. EARLIER DAY MODEL GUIDANCE WAS TOO AGGRESSIVE IN BOTH HEATING AND MOIST ADVECTION INTO THE REGION. DESPITE THE CONCERNS REGARDING THE POTENTIAL FOR SURFACE-BASED STORMS...THE STRONGER ELEVATED STORMS ACROSS CNTRL MN WILL LIKELY INTENSIFY OWING TO STEEPENING MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND AMPLE CLOUD LAYER SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF ROTATION/HAIL GROWTH. THE RECENT RUNS OF THE HRRR SEEM REASONABLE IN ITS DEPICTION OF BOTH GRADUAL STORM STRENGTHENING AND STORMS MOVING EWD INTO NWRN WI EARLY THIS EVENING. THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS WILL BE CAPABLE OF AN ISOLD LARGE HAIL THREAT THROUGH EARLY EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS ACROSS WRN AND CNTRL ND. LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER CELLS. WW ISSUANCE MAY BECOME NECESSARY ESPECIALLY ONCE CELL COVERAGE BEGINS TO INCREASE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 996 MB LOW OVER FAR SE MT WITH A TROUGH OF LOW PRESSURE EXTENDING NWD ACROSS FAR ERN MT NEAR THE ND LINE. LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND INSTABILITY HAVE BEEN STEADILY INCREASING ALONG THE SFC TROUGH LATE THIS AFTERNOON. MLCAPE IS NOW ESTIMATED IN THE 1000 TO 1500 J/KG RANGE BY RAP DATA AND IS FORECAST TO INCREASE MORE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. IN ADDITION...THE EXIT REGION OF A 50 TO 65 KT MID-LEVEL JET WILL OVERSPREAD THE NRN HIGH PLAINS EARLY THIS EVENING. THIS SHOULD HELP TO INCREASE LIFT AND MAINTAIN STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR ALREADY IN PLACE. REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS CURRENTLY SHOW 0-6 KM SHEAR VALUES ABOVE 60 KT IN MUCH OF THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. THIS COMBINED WITH 850 TO 500 MB LAPSE RATES NEAR 8.5 C/KM EVIDENT ON FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOULD SUPPORT SUPERCELL AND LARGE HAIL DEVELOPMENT EARLY THIS EVENING. AS LARGE-SCALE ASCENT CONTINUES TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS...SCATTERED STRONG THUNDERSTORMS SHOULD INITIATE. THIS WILL ALSO FAVOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF WIND DAMAGE AS CELLS MATURE...MOVING EWD INTO INCREASING INSTABILITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLD LARGE TO VERY LARGE HAIL THREAT WILL LIKELY CONTINUE FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THE ISSUANCE OF A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH WILL BE PREDICATED ON THE LARGE HAIL THREAT BECOMING MORE ABUNDANT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 0055Z RADAR ANALYSIS FROM KMPX AND WDSS-II 9 KM CAPPI AND MESH DATA SHOW THE LONG-LIVED SUPERCELL OVER ERN WASHBURN COUNTY WI MOVING EWD INTO SAWYER COUNTY WITH AN ATTENDANT 2 INCH DIAMETER OR LARGER HAIL THREAT. UPSTREAM OF THE NWRN WI SUPERCELL IS AN ORGANIZED BAND OF HYBRID SUPERCELL/QLCS ROTATIONAL STRUCTURES. ALL OF THIS ACTIVITY REMAINS TO THE N OF A NEARLY STATIONARY WARM FRONT GENERALLY 50-100 MI S OF THE ONGOING STORMS. SURFACE TEMPS INVOF THE UPDRAFTS ARE HOVERING AROUND 70 DEG AND ARE CONTRIBUTING TO LARGE SBCINH /MODIFYING THE 04/00Z MPX RAOB/ AND THE ELEVATED CHARACTER OF THE STORMS. DESPITE THE LOW-LEVEL THERMODYNAMIC CONCERNS FOR A SURFACE-BASED STORM THREAT...SOME POTENTIAL APPEARS TO STILL EXIST FOR PERHAPS AN ISOLD WIND DAMAGE RISK WITH THE EVOLVING CONVECTIVE BAND AS IT CONTINUES TO GROW UPSCALE. THE MOST LIKELY AREAS OF SEVERE CONCERN WILL REMAIN WITH THE SUPERCELL AHEAD OF THE LINE AND A WIND/HAIL THREAT ON THE SRN PORTION OF THE CONVECTIVE BAND DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT ONGOING ACROSS WW 490 WILL LIKELY CONTINUE THROUGH LATE THIS EVENING. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE PRIMARY THREATS. THE THREAT SHOULD SPREAD INTO THE CNTRL AND ERN PART OF THE WATCH OVER THE NEXT 2 TO 3 HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE HAS MARKEDLY INCREASED OVER THE LAST FEW HOURS ACROSS FAR NW ND WITH ONE PERSISTENTLY SEVERE CELL LOCATED IN WILLIAMS COUNTY ND. OTHER STRONG CELLS ARE LOCATED ALONG THE MT-ND STATELINE. THIS ACTIVITY IS MOVING EWD ALONG A GRADIENT OF INSTABILITY WHERE MLCAPE VALUES ARE ESTIMATED IN THE 500 TO 1000 J/KG RANGE BY THE RAP. IN ADDITION...THE 00Z SOUNDING AT GLASGOW MT AND BISMARCK ND SHOW STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PROFILES WHICH SHOULD CONTINUE TO FAVOR SEVERE STORM ORGANIZATION AND POSSIBLY SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL. THE LATEST HRRR MAINTAINS CONVECTIVE COVERAGE AND DEVELOPS A SHORT BOWING LINE SEGMENT. THIS LINE IS FORECAST TO MOVE TO NEAR MINOT ND BY 04Z. IF CELLS CAN ORGANIZE INTO A COLD POOL AS THE HRRR SUGGESTS IS POSSIBLE...THEN THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT WOULD LIKELY INCREASE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS ACROSS THE CNTRL PART OF WW 490.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD CONTINUE ACROSS THE SERN PART OF WW 491 FOR A FEW MORE HOURS. AS THE LINE MOVES SEWD TOWARD THE EDGE OF WW 491 TOWARD MIDNIGHT...THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE ISOLATED. FOR THIS REASON...ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SHORT BOWING LINE SEGMENT IN DUNN...CHIPPEWA AND TAYLOR COUNTIES WI IS LOCATED ALONG A SFC PRESSURE PERTURBATION AND APPEARS TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH A SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH EVIDENT ON WATER VAPOR IMAGERY. MLCAPE IN THE SRN PART OF WW 491 IS ESTIMATED TO BE AROUND 1500 J/KG WITH REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS SHOWING ABOUT 40 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR. THIS SHOULD CONTINUE TO SUPPORT AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT LATE THIS EVENING AS THE LINE MOVES SEWD. A TURN MORE TO THE SOUTH IS POSSIBLE AS THE CELL PROPAGATION FAVORS THE MORE UNSTABLE AIRMASS NEAR THE MS RIVER. ALTHOUGH THE ACTIVITY IS MOSTLY SFC-BASED...A CAP IS FORECAST TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS MAKING THE STORMS ELEVATED. THIS FACTOR ALONG WITH A SLOW DECREASE IN INSTABILITY SHOULD MAKE THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT ASSOCIATED WITH THE LINE MORE MARGINAL WITH TIME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS ARE EXPECTED TO PERSIST TONIGHT AND EVENTUALLY EXTEND INTO NRN MN. A NEW SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH APPEARS LIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SEVERE STORMS PRODUCING HAIL CURRENTLY EXIST ACROSS CNTRL ND IN A ZONE OF WARM ADVECTION ON THE NOSE OF THE LOW LEVEL JET...AND BENEATH INCREASING FLOW ALOFT WITH THE UPPER TROUGH. FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL CONTINUE TO FAVOR FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE STORMS TONIGHT FROM ND INTO MN...AND PERHAPS NERN SD. VERY STEEP LAPSE RATES AS WELL AS A ZONE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY JUST UPSTREAM WILL FUEL SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL. DAMAGING WINDS WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE AS STORMS MERGE INTO BOWS...POSSIBLY WITH CONTINUED SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS AND DESPITE SOME CONVECTIVE INHIBITION IN THE BOUNDARY LAYER. HODOGRAPHS ARE QUITE LONG...AND SHOULD EASILY SUPPORT ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS GIVEN THE INSTABILITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A HAIL AND WIND THREAT PERSISTS ACROSS SERN ND AND N CNTRL MN. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR THE ADDITION OF ANOTHER WATCH ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF NRN N CNTRL MN AND PERHAPS FAR NWRN WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SERIES OF SUPERCELLS CONTINUES TO MARCH EWD IN A SEMI-ELEVATED FASHION ON THE NOSE OF THE LOW-LEVEL JET AND JUST AHEAD OF THE SURFACE LOW CENTERED NEAR SISSETON. ALTHOUGH THE SURFACE AIR IS A BIT COOL N OF THE WARM FRONT...COLD HAIL-LADEN CORES AS WELL AS MESOCYCLONIC CIRCULATIONS WILL LIKELY ENHANCE WIND POTENTIAL. VERY LARGE HAIL WILL CONTINUE TO BE POSSIBLE...AS WELL AS HEAVY RAINS IN EXCESS OF 2 IN/HR. THESE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO REMAIN 25-50 MILES N OF THE SURFACE WARM FRONT AS THEY TRAVEL ESEWD THIS MORNING. ANOTHER WATCH MAY BE NEEDED TO THE EAST OF WW 492 IF CURRENT TRENDS HOLD AS EXPECTED. ..JEWELL.. 09/04/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
